scorecard.note: The planned visuals are far too abstract and rely on a conceptual 'Data' character that would be extremely difficult to render clearly and quickly on a phone screen. The visuals need to be concrete and instantly understandable representatio

storyboard.ears: Indonesia gets the fame. America has the volcanoes.
The US tops the world with 165 volcanoes. Indonesia, everyone's guess, is only fourth, so fame is not the same as count.
storyboard.eyes: substance: glowing orange lava; cause: Data hammers a survey stake at the foot of each volcano and it erupts, counted one by one down the chain
storyboard.evidence: Smithsonian Institution | Holocene (last ~11,700 years) volcanoes by country | https://volcano.si.edu/volcanolist_countries.cfm | 2026-08-19

storyboard.ears: Alaska alone holds 130 of them. That's more than Indonesia's whole total, so one cold state outdoes a famous volcano nation.
storyboard.evidence: U.S. Geological Survey / Smithsonian Institution | Where the US's 165 volcanoes actually are | https://www.usgs.gov/observatories/avo | 2026-08-19

storyboard.ears: Three in four of Earth's volcanoes sit on the Ring of Fire. That's why Alaska, Japan and Indonesia all rank so high.
storyboard.eyes: substance: red-hot lava; cause: Data paddles a canoe around the ring and each volcano he reaches erupts with lava
storyboard.evidence: U.S. Geological Survey | Share of Earth's active volcanoes on the Ring of Fire | https://www.usgs.gov/media/images/ringoffiregif | 2026-08-19

storyboard.ears: Next time you trust your gut, check the count first. Fame and numbers rarely match.
